title: Efficient Certificates of Anti-Concentration Beyond Gaussians
authors: Ainesh Bakshi (MIT, USA), Pravesh K. Kothari (IAS, USA), Goutham Rajendran (CMU, USA), Madhur Tulsiani (TTIC, USA), Aravindan Vijayaraghavan (Northwestern, USA)
abstract: A set of high dimensional points in isotropic position is said to be anti-concentrated if for every direction, the fraction of points projected along that direction with small magnitude is small. Motivated by applications to list-decodable learning and clustering, three recent works considered the problem of constructing efficient certificates of anti-concentration, when the points are sampled from the Gaussian distribution. Their certificates played a crucial role in several algorithmic statistics results including list-decodable learning and settling the robust learnability of Gaussian mixtures. However, these certificates remain limited to rotationally invariant distributions and affine transformations thereof. This work presents a new formulation of anti-concentration. Using this formulation, we obtain quasi-polynomial time verifiable sum-of-squares certificates of anti-concentration that hold for a wide class of distributions, including anti-concentrated product distributions, uniform distributions over ell-p balls and affine transformations thereof. Consequently our method upgrades and extends results in algorithmic statistics, eg. list-decodable learning and clustering to all such distributions. As in the case of previous works, our certificates are also obtained via relaxations in the sum-of-squares hierarchy. However, the nature of our argument differs significantly from prior works that formulate anticoncentration as the non-negativity of an explicit polynomial. Our argument constructs a canonical integer program for anti-concentration and analysis a SoS relaxation of it, independent of the intended application. The explicit polynomials appearing in prior works can be seen as specific dual certificates to this program. From a technical standpoint, unlike existing works that explicitly construct sum-of-squares certificates, our argument relies on duality and analyzes a pseudoexpectation on large subsets of the input points that take a small value in some direction. Our analysis uses the method of polynomial reweightings to reduce the problem to analyzing only analytically dense or sparse directions.
